```{r ks-values}
mp <- function(g) main_peak[genome == g]
om <- function(s) orth_sum[split == s, Ks_median]
op <- function(s) orth_sum[split == s, Ks_peak]
abs_rhi <- c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "ggRhiOryz1")
mort_mid <- peaks[genome %in% gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome] & Ks > 1.5 & Ks < 3]
av <- function(nd, col) anc_show[node == nd][[col]]
deep_sat <- orth_sum[split %in% c("Mucorales / Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales / Mortierellales"), range(Ks_median)]
gl_pre <- paste0(gsub(".", "_", of_names[["gzAbsGlau1"]], fixed = TRUE), "_")
has_gla <- function(x) vapply(strsplit(x, ", ", fixed = TRUE), function(v) any(startsWith(v, gl_pre)), FALSE)
gla_both <- function(nd) round(100 * sup[node == nd, mean(has_gla(genes1) & has_gla(genes2))])
```

- **Where Ks saturates.** Ortholog Ks rises with split age and then levels
off (`r fig("ks_ridges")`B). Splits younger than about age 90 (relative time,
root = 1,000) have median Ks
`r paste(sprintf("%.2f", orth_sum[age < 90, range(Ks_median)]), collapse = "-")`
in all three orders, for example
`r om("Within Mortierellales (M. zonata / L. schmuckeri)")` for the
Mortierellales split at age 68 and
`r om("Within Mucor (M. fragilis / M. velutinosus)")` for the *Mucor* split
at age 71, so synonymous rates are similar for young splits. Older splits
diverge: the median reaches about 2 at age 122 in *Cunninghamella*
(`r om("Within Cunninghamella (C. blakesleeana / C. echinulata)")`), but only
at ages 194-195 in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus*
(`r om("Within Absidia (A. repens / A. glauca)")` and
`r om("Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. stolonifer)")`), while a *Mucor* split
at age 175 is already mostly saturated
(`r om("Within Mucor (M. flavus / M. piriformis)")`), as are the Mortierellales
splits at ages 222-238 (the tree has no Mortierellales splits between ages 90
and 220). Every split from age 280 to the root has a median Ks of
`r paste(sprintf("%.1f", orth_sum[age >= 280, range(Ks_median)]), collapse = "-")`,
whatever its age. Ks therefore carries age information up to Ks about 2
(shaded in `r fig("ks_ridges")`A), but the split age at which that limit is
reached differs between lineages by more than 1.5-fold, even within Mucorales,
so Ks values of older events cannot be converted to ages or compared between
lineages.
- ***Absidia* and *Rhizopus*.** Their segmental pairs have a main Ks
  component at `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", range(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, Ks])), collapse = "-")`
  holding `r paste(pct(range(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, weight])), collapse = "-")`%
  of the pairs (`r fig("ks_ridges")`, `r tab("peaks")`), and their ancestral-SD
  duplicates have a median Ks of `r av("N46", "median_Ks")` and
  `r av("N32", "median_Ks")` (`r fig("anc_ks")`). Both events are younger than
  the split of the two genera (ortholog Ks `r om("Absidia / Rhizopus")`), so
  they are independent. The gene trees place the *Rhizopus* event before the
  split of *R. oryzae* and *R. stolonifer*.
- **Ks cannot order these WGDs and the nearest speciations.** The paralog peaks
  lie within about 0.3 of the ortholog peaks of the splits from *A. glauca*
  (`r sprintf("%.2f", op("Within Absidia (A. repens / A. glauca)"))`) and from
  *R. stolonifer* (`r sprintf("%.2f", op("Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. stolonifer)"))`;
  `r tab("orthks")`). At Ks near 2 such differences are within the noise,
  and two effects pull paralog Ks below the true age of a WGD: rediploidization
  completed only after the speciation in part of the genome (shown for
  *Absidia*), and the codon-usage bias of retained duplicates, which are often
  highly expressed. The order therefore comes from the gene trees, which put
  both WGDs before these splits; Ks shows only that each WGD happened shortly
  before the speciation. (The median ortholog Ks, `r om("Within Absidia (A. repens / A. glauca)")`
  and `r om("Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. stolonifer)")`, overstates these
  splits, because saturated orthologs pull it up.)
- **One *Absidia* WGD, partly rediploidized after a speciation.** The *Absidia*
  duplications fall on two branches, before and after *A. glauca* diverged
  (`r fig("anc_branches")`). *A. glauca* has both copies of
  `r gla_both("N40")`% of the duplications placed before its split, so these
  are shared. It lies outside the duplications placed after its split, but in
  many of these families its own copies form a separate duplication on the
  *A. glauca* branch, and these pairs are younger (median Ks of ancestral-SD
  pairs `r av("N46", "median_Ks")` against `r av("N40", "median_Ks")`). This
  is the pattern of a single WGD whose rediploidization was completed for part
  of the genome only after the speciation (lineage-specific ohnolog
  resolution, as after the salmonid WGD), not of a second round; *A. glauca*
  has also lost more copies or has a less complete annotation (details in the
  extended report).
- **Mortierellales.** All `r uniqueN(mort_mid$genome)` Mortierellales genomes
  have a segmental Ks component at
  `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", range(mort_mid$Ks)), collapse = "-")`, and the
  ancestral-SD pairs of the Mortierellales stem are enriched in this range
  (`r av("N10", "Ks_1.5_2.6")`% between Ks 1.5 and 2.6, against
  `r av("N10", "Ks_1.5_2.6_other")`% for the other stem duplicates;
  `r fig("ks_ridges")`A). The gene trees place the event before the
  Mortierellales crown (age 280), yet this component has a lower Ks than the
  orthologs of the crown splits, which are mostly saturated
  (`r fig("ks_ridges")`B): the same discrepancy as for *Absidia* and
  *Rhizopus*, but larger. Ks therefore cannot date the event or compare it
  with the Mucorales WGDs. That it still leaves an unsaturated component
  suggests that it happened late on the long Mortierellales stem, as close to
  the crown as the gene trees allow, but this is tentative.
- **Mucorales stem.** Its ancestral-SD pairs are saturated (median Ks
  `r av("N12", "median_Ks")`; `r av("N12", "Ks_below_2")`% below 2), as is the
  divergence between the orders (median ortholog Ks
  `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", deep_sat), collapse = "-")`), so Ks cannot date this
  event.

# Conclusions {-}

```{r summary-fig, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = cap("summary", paste0("Summary of the large-scale duplication events on the dated species tree (relative time, root = 1,000), with the node labels used in the text (", fig("ref_tree"), "). Clades without an event are collapsed into triangles (number of genomes in brackets). Numbered markers sit on the branches where the gene trees place the duplications; filled markers are events with block (ancestral-SD) and Ks evidence, the open marker a weaker block signal. Shaded: the time window in which Ks can still rank events (roughly the last 300 units); events 3 and 4 fall within it, Ks tentatively places event 2 late on the Mortierellales stem (bar; see Section 5), whereas event 1 is beyond it."))}
ev <- data.table(
  id = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
  node = c(mrca(gen[order == "Mucorales", genome]), mrca(gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome]),
           mrca(c("AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1")),
           mrca(c("ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1")), mrca(gen[order != "Mortierellales", genome])),
  strong = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
ev[, `:=`(x = d0$branch[match(node, d0$node)], y = d0$y[match(node, d0$node)])]
# Event 2: Ks tentatively places it late on the Mortierellales stem
mort_crown_x <- d0$x[match(mrca(gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome]), d0$node)]
ev[id == "2", x := mort_crown_x - 60]
ev_col <- accent
datable_age <- 300   # roughly the age up to which Ks ranks events (see Section 5)
p_tree <- p_base +
  annotate("segment", x = mort_crown_x - 120, xend = mort_crown_x, y = ev[id == "2", y], yend = ev[id == "2", y],
           linewidth = 3.5, colour = ev_col, alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_point(data = ev, aes(x, y, fill = strong), shape = 21, size = 7, colour = ev_col, stroke = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = ev, aes(x, y, label = id, colour = strong), size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = ev_col, `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = ev_col), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, 250), labels = rev(seq(0, 1000, 250))) +
  labs(x = "Relative time before present (root = 1,000)") +
  theme(axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "grey40"), axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "grey40"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9.5, hjust = 0.3))
# Shaded window where Ks can still rank events, drawn beneath the tree
datable <- annotate("rect", xmin = 1000 - datable_age, xmax = 1000, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
                    fill = accent, alpha = 0.07)
p_tree$layers <- c(datable, p_tree$layers)
p_tree <- p_tree + annotate("text", x = 1000 - datable_age / 2, y = max(d0$y) + 0.9,
                            label = "Ks-datable", size = 3, colour = accent)
# Evidence per event
abs_ks <- main_peak[genome %in% c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1"), median(Ks)]
rhi_ks <- main_peak[genome == "ggRhiOryz1", Ks]
ev_txt <- data.table(
  id = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"), strong = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE),
  title = c("Mucorales stem (N12): ancient large-scale duplication",
            "Mortierellales stem (N10): large-scale duplication",
            "Absidia (N40, N46): recent WGD, before the A. glauca split",
            "R. oryzae + R. stolonifer (N32): recent WGD",
            "Umbelopsidales + Mucorales stem (N9): weaker block signal"),
  text = c(sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications (%d%%) in %d genomes; blocks eroded (%d%% dispersed today); Ks saturated",
                   fmt_n(ac("N12", "ancientSD")), anc_pct("N12"), ac("N12", "genomes"),
                   round(100 * ac("N12", "DD") / ac("N12", "classified"))),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications (%d%%); collinear blocks partly retained; unsaturated Ks component %.1f-%.1f: probably late on the stem",
                   fmt_n(ac("N10", "ancientSD")), anc_pct("N10"), min(mort_mid$Ks), max(mort_mid$Ks)),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications; Ks peak %.1f; rediploidization partly completed after the A. glauca split (LORe-like)",
                   fmt_n(ac("N40", "ancientSD") + ac("N46", "ancientSD")), abs_ks),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications; Ks peak %.1f; after the split from R. microsporus",
                   fmt_n(ac("N32", "ancientSD")), rhi_ks),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications: %s shared with Umbelopsidales (both copies), %s likely Mucorales-stem duplications placed too deep",
                   fmt_n(ac("N9", "ancientSD")), fmt_n(e5s("both", "anc")), fmt_n(e5s("one", "anc")))))
ev_txt[, row := rev(seq_len(.N))]
p_txt <- ggplot(ev_txt) +
  geom_point(aes(0, row, fill = strong), shape = 21, size = 7, colour = ev_col, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(0, row, label = id, colour = strong), size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(0.06, row + 0.14, label = title), hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3) +
  geom_text(aes(0.06, row - 0.02, label = stringr::str_wrap(text, 62)), hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 2.9,
            lineheight = 0.95, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = ev_col, `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = ev_col), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.03, 1)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.2, nrow(ev_txt) + 0.5)) +
  theme_void()
p_tree + p_txt + plot_layout(widths = c(1.35, 1))
```

- **An ancient large-scale duplication shared by all Mucorales.**
  `r fmt_n(ac("N12", "ancientSD"))` gene-tree duplications on the Mucorales
  stem arose in duplicated blocks; their copies survive in
  `r ac("N12", "genomes")` of the 42 Mucorales genomes but are now mostly
  dispersed, because gene order has been scrambled since. The event is older
  than Ks can resolve. The signal is concentrated on the Mucorales stem: the
  branch shared with Umbelopsidales and the root of Mucoromycota carry fewer
  duplications and a smaller share of ancestral-SD ones, so the event most
  likely postdates the split from Umbelopsidales. Half of the ancestral-SD
  duplications on the shared branch look like Mucorales-stem duplications
  placed one branch too deep; the rest are a weaker block signal shared with
  Umbelopsidales. This matches, and places more precisely, the WGD
  proposed by Corrochano et al. (2016).
- **Lineage-specific large-scale duplications.** Two recent, independent
  events in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus* (Ks about 1.6-1.9), with many collinear
  blocks still intact; and an event on the Mortierellales stem
  (`r fmt_n(ac("N10", "ancientSD"))` ancestral-SD duplications) placed by
  the gene trees before the Mortierellales crown; its unsaturated Ks component
  (near 2.4) suggests a late position on the stem, but Ks cannot compare its
  age with the Mucorales events, because synonymous rates differ between
  lineages at that depth.
- **WGD or several segmental duplications.** These analyses show block
  duplications on each branch but cannot tell a single WGD from several large
  segmental duplications. A model-based test (Whale) is planned.

# Supplementary figures {-}

```{r figure-s1, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 10, fig.cap = "**Figure S1.** How gene-tree duplications are classified as ancestral-SD, with the number of duplications or copy pairs at each step (all branches of the species tree). Box colour: where the step comes from (OrthoFinder, doubletrouble, or this study). Copy pairs are counted within genomes, so one duplication contributes pairs in every descendant genome that kept both copies. Near-identical pairs are excluded from both synteny tests. Pairs that are not doubletrouble pairs (not among the top 5 within-genome DIAMOND hits) cannot pass either test but are part of the final dataset when their duplication is ancestral-SD. Expected by chance: mean number of ancestral-SD duplications over 3 runs with shuffled gene order (neighbourhood test only). Percentages in the final box are shares of the ancestral-SD copy pairs by the order of the genome they lie in. MucCirc3 has no copy pairs: its gene identifiers in the OrthoFinder results could not be matched to its annotation."}
# Counts for each step of the ancestral-SD classification
fl_pairs <- unique(anc[, .(genome, key, event, type, Ks, nb_pass, syn, cls)])
fl_pairs[, `:=`(dt_pair = !is.na(type), near = !is.na(type) & (is.na(Ks) | Ks < 0.05))]
fl_ev <- unique(anc[, .(event, syn_genomes, cls)])
fl_null <- ev_null[, .(anc = sum(n_genomes >= 2)), by = run][, mean(anc)]
fl_final <- unique(fl_pairs[cls == "ancientSD", .(genome, key)])[, order := as.character(gen$order[match(genome, gen$genome)])]
fl <- list(
  of_all = nrow(dups), of_sup = nrow(sup_int),
  ev = nrow(fl_ev), pairs = nrow(fl_pairs), pair_genomes = uniqueN(fl_pairs$genome),
  dt = fl_pairs[, sum(dt_pair)], dt_near = fl_pairs[, sum(near)], not_dt = fl_pairs[, sum(!dt_pair)],
  sd = fl_pairs[, sum(type %in% "SD" & !near)], nb_tested = fl_pairs[, sum(!is.na(nb_pass))],
  nb_pass = fl_pairs[, sum(nb_pass %in% TRUE)], both = fl_pairs[, sum(type %in% "SD" & !near & nb_pass %in% TRUE)],
  syn = fl_pairs[, sum(syn)], syn_genomes = fl_pairs[syn == TRUE, uniqueN(genome)],
  ev0 = fl_ev[, sum(syn_genomes == 0)], ev1 = fl_ev[, sum(syn_genomes == 1)], ev2 = fl_ev[, sum(syn_genomes >= 2)],
  final_pairs = nrow(fl_final), final_genomes = uniqueN(fl_final$genome))
fl_ord <- fl_final[, .N, by = order][order(-N)]
pc <- function(n, d) sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", fmt_n(n), 100 * n / d)

src_cols <- c(OrthoFinder = "grey35", doubletrouble = "#1B9E77", "This study" = accent)
src_fill <- c(OrthoFinder = "grey93", doubletrouble = "#DDF1EB", "This study" = "#EFE6F3")
bx <- rbindlist(list(
  list(1, 50, 100, 60, 7, "OrthoFinder gene-tree duplications",
       sprintf("%s duplications in all gene trees", fmt_n(fl$of_all)), "OrthoFinder"),
  list(2, 50, 88, 60, 9, "1. Supported duplications on internal branches",
       sprintf("Support \u2265 0.5 (both copies kept in at least half of the descendant species),\non branches of the 61-genome species tree: %s duplications", fmt_n(fl$of_sup)), "OrthoFinder"),
  list(3, 50, 75, 60, 9, "2. Copy pairs",
       sprintf("One copy from each side of a duplication, in the same genome:\n%s copy pairs from %s duplications, in %d genomes",
               fmt_n(fl$pairs), fmt_n(fl$ev), fl$pair_genomes), "This study"),
  list(4, 30, 61, 48, 9, "3. Synteny tests, on doubletrouble duplicate pairs",
       sprintf("Within-genome DIAMOND top-5 hits: %s copy pairs\n%s near-identical (Ks < 0.05 or none): not tested",
               pc(fl$dt, fl$pairs), fmt_n(fl$dt_near)), "doubletrouble"),
  list(5, 79, 61, 34, 9, "Not doubletrouble pairs",
       sprintf("%s copy pairs: no Ks or class,\ncannot pass 3a or 3b; kept in step 5", pc(fl$not_dt, fl$pairs)), "This study"),
  list(6, 15, 47, 32, 9, "3a. Segmental (SD)",
       sprintf("Collinear block, \u2265 5 anchors (MCScanX),\nKs \u2265 0.05: %s copy pairs", fmt_n(fl$sd)), "doubletrouble"),
  list(7, 50, 47, 34, 9, "3b. Neighbourhood-syntenic",
       sprintf("\u2265 2 other families link the windows of\n10 genes around each copy: %s of %s tested", fmt_n(fl$nb_pass), fmt_n(fl$nb_tested)), "This study"),
  list(8, 32, 34, 60, 7, "Syntenic copy pairs (3a or 3b)",
       sprintf("%s copy pairs (%s pass both), in %d genomes", fmt_n(fl$syn), fmt_n(fl$both), fl$syn_genomes), "This study"),
  list(9, 50, 21, 60, 9, "4. In how many genomes is each duplication syntenic?",
       "For each duplication: the number of descendant genomes\nwith at least one syntenic copy pair (3a or 3b)", "This study"),
  list(10, 14, 9, 26, 7, "None", sprintf("%s duplications", pc(fl$ev0, fl$ev)), "This study"),
  list(11, 42, 9, 26, 7, "One genome", sprintf("%s duplications", pc(fl$ev1, fl$ev)), "This study"),
  list(12, 76, 9, 38, 7, "Two or more genomes: ancestral-SD",
       sprintf("%s duplications\n(expected by chance: %s)", pc(fl$ev2, fl$ev), fmt_n(round(fl_null))), "This study"),
  list(13, 50, -7, 80, 11, "5. Final dataset: ancestral-SD duplications",

setnames(bx, c("id", "x", "y", "w", "h", "title", "body", "src"))
